quarterly_data.signal: CEO Michael Hurlston on gross margin: 'We expect gross margin expansion to continue, driven by product mix and tight operational execution.' On repricing: 'we did reprice a little bit. I think most of our LTAs are more forward-looking in terms of the price impact'; pricing gave some benefit on the gross margin line and 'still has some room to play through', while 'the long pole this quarter was more on mix, where we were shipping a lot more of our high-mix components' - 'we think we have some room to run on the gross margin line'.

Financial targets: CEO Michael Hurlston - 'we will come out with some new financial targets probably at the next OFC. We are obviously running well ahead on almost every metric, on revenue, on margin, on operating margin.' NPO and CW lasers are 'new things that we did not factor into our discussion at OFC', and OCS 'seems to be doing a bit better than expected'; on adding to the guide, 'We think we have the opportunity to do that more as we look out in future quarters.' CFO Wajid Ali: the operating-margin guideline given at $2 billion of revenue was 38%-42%, already reached at its midpoint at much lower revenue levels - 'Think of the 42% outlier more as a midpoint, with the range probably moving up 100-200 basis points versus what we showed at OFC.' At the midpoint, the Q1 FY2027 operating-margin guide represents an expansion of more than 2,100 basis points year-over-year.
quarterly_data.figure: $2B-revenue operating-margin model 38%-42%, range probably up 100-200 bps; new targets probably at the next OFC

quarterly_data.signal: CPO / NPO timing (CEO Michael Hurlston): Lumentum is already shipping its lead CPO customer for scale-out; 'for scale-up, we expect to be shipping in the second half of calendar 2027 for their deliveries in 2028', and 'Our leading customers on NPO, plus or minus, probably maybe minus a quarter, are in that ZIP code.' The first couple of NPO engagements use the same kind of ELS high-powered laser, possibly followed by a couple with a mid-power laser integrated inside the optical engine; the ones with the best line of sight and sooner timing are the high-powered type. No retrofit: 'I don't think there are existing TPUs, XPUs, GPUs that are shipping that have a fast enough SERDES speed' for NPO or CPO; new GPU / XPU / TPU silicon arriving from mid-2027 through early 2028 drives SerDes speeds consistent with NPO or CPO adoption. Wupen Yuen: 'there is a 2028 event for optical scale-up', with new processors and new racks; for NPO optical engines Lumentum scales its 400 mW design principle to the 150 mW-200 mW range.
quarterly_data.figure: scale-up laser shipments H2 CY2027 for 2028 deliveries; NPO leaders possibly a quarter earlier; new silicon mid-2027 to early 2028

quarterly_data.signal: NPO standards (CEO Michael Hurlston): OCI and other standards for the interface between the ASIC and the optical engine are 'great for us because that opens up switch opportunities, for example, that may not be open to us before'; Lumentum is engaged in both standards-based and custom NPO, and the custom implementations are 'really going to be our first wave of NPO engagement.' Wupen Yuen: the next generation will be OCI/MSA based on the optical side, while form factors stay proprietary and differ from customer to customer.

Laser economics: CEO Michael Hurlston - 'Lasers are one of our better businesses, and the lasers are corporate accretive, whether it's CW or EML', with 'no slowdown at all in the demand that we are seeing from EML.' Wupen Yuen: much of today's 200G-per-lane volume is on 800G, where EML share is much higher than CW share, and 'EML will remain a very important player in 200G-per-lane'; the new, more efficient 200G CW laser design 'gave us a much better gross margin profile.'

Systems supply (CEO Michael Hurlston): 'pockets of supply chain tightness for certain components cap shipments below total market demand', while the factories executed to the aggressive plan for both cloud transceivers and OCS; the bulk of Q4 cloud transceiver shipments were at 800G, and 1.6T transceivers began shipping as planned.

OCS customers and execution (CEO Michael Hurlston): 'We are continuing to ship to a number of different customers'; the supply-chain problems early in the ramp are behind ('We are out of that now'), and on software, where he had expected more difficulty, 'we have done well'. 'we are the only ones that have a track record outside of a contract manufacturing relationship with a large OCS user', and as the only merchant OCS supplier Lumentum expects 'to get every single call and have the first look, I think, at every single opportunity out there.'
